reviewed_by: Codex focused review for Project permission modes and explicit policy feedback
reason: Policy, API, MCP, browser, command runtime, harness, and UI changes make destination authorization distinct from approval and add an explicit permission bypass. Fifteen policy cases cover risk versus network effect, target and port boundaries, public DNS, time, and bypass; twelve focused Core cases cover persistence, MCP and broker classification, model-visible refusal, frozen harness permissions, command network boundaries, browser scope, and web-search disclosure. Fifty-five frontend cases cover authorization-mode confirmation, browser scope and reload, and settings hydration. Two native cases cover all-destination and bypass proxy behavior plus URL-only CONNECT. Five mocked and eight real-Core Project policy journeys cover desktop and the applicable 320/390/430 mobile Chromium/WebKit profiles, including production LAN save, authenticated re-entry, revocation, and command-session policy persistence.
exclusions: No full Python, frontend, native, or Playwright suite was authorized. Unrelated provider, mission, SSH, and browser journeys are excluded; their shared policy boundaries are covered in the selected Core and UI cases. Native proxy tests are exact unit cases, not a packaged desktop app run. Physical-device browser checks and live Mercury behavior are outside isolated CI and require separate deployment verification. The local Python environment uses the working 3.11 repository venv; CI uses its default 3.12.
